The strategy accounts for all actual transitive proof uses, hypotheses, well-definedness, direction, and choice strength. Remove finitely many disjoint coordinate discs about the poles. Cover the remaining compact smooth bordered domain by finitely many holomorphic coordinate charts and subdivide it into finitely many chart-contained piecewise smooth cells, matching edge subdivisions on both sides. In each chart integrate div(u grad v-v grad u)=u Delta v-v Delta u by the elementary planar Green formula (first prove it on graph-bounded rectangles by Fubini, then add finitely many cells). On overlaps a holomorphic change of chart multiplies the Laplacian and area density by reciprocal factors, while the outward conormal line integral is unchanged; hence the identity is intrinsic. Interior edge integrals cancel in opposite orientations. When u,v are harmonic off the removed discs, the area integral is zero; the remaining boundary terms are the outer boundary and the small circles. Smoothness of the outer boundary gives the usual conormal there, and if u=v=0 on that boundary its contribution vanishes. This finite-cell argument is choice free and proves the needed special surface Green identity directly, without importing the out-of-plan general Stokes page.
